title: Volume
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
about: Teacher-verified mastery check. Written separately from the practice generators: different wordings, word problems, and an 'is this right?' item. Each item is worth 1 point. 'math' is the calculation in JavaScript form (answers in terms of π give the number in front of π), or 'yes'/'no'; the test checks the answer key's number against it.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a box 6 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm.
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 m and height 7 m, in terms of π.
Find the volume of a cylinder with diameter 4 in and height 10 in, in terms of π.
Find the volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 8 cm, in terms of π.
A shoebox is 12 in long, 6 in wide and 4 in tall. How much does it hold?
Dev says a 2 by 3 by 4 box has volume 9. Is he right? Explain, and find the volume.
Find the volume of a box 8 ft by 5 ft by 2 ft.
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 2 cm and height 9 cm, in terms of π.
Find the volume of a cylinder with diameter 6 m and height 5 m, in terms of π.
Find the volume of a cone with radius 6 in and height 5 in, in terms of π.
A fish tank is 20 in long, 10 in wide and 12 in tall. How much water does it hold?
Mia says a cone with radius 3 cm and height 4 cm has volume 36π cm³. Is she right? Explain, and find the volume.
items.answer: 12π cm³ (No: a cone is one third of the cylinder)
